text:
Dina: Kicking off Silverline -> Redwood POC thread. Customer wants a drop-in proxy so their integrators don't change code. Need parity checklist, security Qs answered, and an initial pricing stance. Staging tokens arriving later today. Who can own what?

Omar: I can lead POC plan + pricing. Quick ask: do we have a canonical example of their streaming frames and non-streaming responses? Need to scope facade mapping effort.

Dina: Example below. Note they rely on `X-SL-Tenant` header and include `deterministic_seed` + `flags` in choices. They also use `delta_text` streaming frames.
```
POST /v1/generate?model=sl-v2
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>, X-SL-Tenant: acct-628
Body: {"prompt":"Explain the graph...","max_tokens":128}

Response (non-stream):
{
  "id":"r_001","trace_id":"trace-55","choices":[{"text":"...","flags":["sensitive"]}],"deterministic_seed":42,"usage":{"prompt_tokens":8,"completion_tokens":20}
}

Stream frames (newline-delimited JSON):
{"delta_text":"Hello"}
{"delta_text":" world"}
{"done":true}
```

Liam: Engineering: our runtime doesn't emit `deterministic_seed` nor `choices[].flags` today. We do have `annotations` on choices. Token counting also differs: Silverline tokenization treats trailing space/newline as token in some cases. We can add a thin facade service to synthesize fields and map streaming frames.

Omar: POC scope suggestion: 1) Accept `X-SL-Tenant` passthrough, 2) Preserve incoming `trace_id` in responses (or copy into X-Orig-Trace header), 3) Synthesize `deterministic_seed` with a stable hash of prompt, 4) Expose `choices[].flags` by translating from `annotations`. Also provide a feature toggle `sl_compat_mode`.

Teja: Security checklist from customer: KMS-managed customer keys, ability to produce full request/response audit logs for 90 days, IP allowlist, idempotency-key support, SOC2 evidence, and mTLS for pilot. Who will own the questionnaire?

Dina: Teja owns security questionnaire and will validate KMS mapping. Liam you'll own the facade PR. Omar drafts pricing and pilot terms; I'll coordinate Legal for NDA/DPA.

Liam: Implementation note: for streaming we will map {"delta_text":"x"} -> Redwood event {"type":"content","chunk":"x"}. Example mapping snippet: 
```js
// pseudo
if (frame.delta_text) emit({type:'content',chunk:frame.delta_text});
if (resp.trace_id) resp.headers['X-Orig-Trace'] = resp.trace_id;
// synth deterministic_seed: hash64(prompt) % 2**31
```
Normalization: to match silverline usage counts, pre-tokenize with normalizeNewlines=true and trim-trailing-space=false. Toggle behind feature flag to avoid global perf impact.

Omar: Pricing: propose POC arrangement: 500k normalized-token credit + 20% pilot discount thereafter for 2 months. For billing during pilot we will bill on normalized tokens (the facade's normalization) so customer's metrics align. I'll produce a one-page quote.

Teja: mTLS is a blocker for hosted API. If they insist on mutual TLS from their integrators to our hosted endpoints we need to confirm whether our hosted edge supports client cert validation per-customer. If not, fall back to Dedicated or Private. Flagging as risk.

Dina: Good catch. Omar, add mTLS to risk section and include Dedicated fallback cost delta. Teja, list the exact cert requirements (CA rotation, cert lifetime) so we can validate.

Liam: Tokenization delta detail: Silverline uses a nonstandard split on consecutive newlines that increases completion_tokens by 1 in ~6% of samples. We'll add normalization step of collapsing triple-newlines to double-newlines only for sl_compat_mode. Perf overhead estimated <2ms per request.

deploy-bot: Provision update: staging VPC vpc-poc-9 created. KMS key `poctest-silverline-2026` created with grants to `eng-team`. Temporary role and creds will be posted to #secure-staging in 90 minutes.

Omar: Timeline proposal: sync tomorrow 9:30am PT, security questionnaire draft by tomorrow noon, facade PR by EOD tomorrow (feature flagged), pricing quote by EOD. Staging smoke test after Legal completes NDA/DPA.

Teja: I'll start the questionnaire now. For the KMS mapping, I need a runbook showing key alias, rotation policy, and how we restrict decrypt/encrypt to the facade service principal. Also want to confirm audit-log retention and redaction behavior.

Dina: Assignments recap: Teja -> security questionnaire + KMS runbook; Liam -> facade implementation + PR (feature flag + streaming mapping); Omar -> POC pricing/terms + risk doc incl. mTLS fallback; Dina -> legal + customer comms.

Liam: One more thing: customer expects `usage` to be presented exactly like Silverline. We'll synthesize usage by running the normalization token counter and then return `usage` with the same keys.

Omar: I'll include billing note that normalized token counts are used for POC only and contract will reconcile on commit.

Dina: Thanks team. We'll pick up 9:30am tomorrow. :rocket:
